messages:
anya: Heads up — seeing a KV prefix warmup regression after yesterday's runtime change.
anya: Quick numbers from the canary traffic: Hosted warmup hit-rate ~72% after 60s, Dedicated ~34%, Private (customer VPC with NFS) ~28%. 95p latency on Dedicated bumped 180ms -> 320ms.
anya: Root cause looks like slower population of local KV caches when backing store is network-mounted. Happened after we changed kernel selection + batching heuristics in rollout.
ben: Which rollout/commit?
anya: runtime@c3f9d2b — kernel-selection: prefer fused-int8 GEMM for transformer blocks; batching: default window increased 20->40 to reduce token-cost.
ben: Hmm. Curious why that would affect warmup hit-rate. Kernel change shouldn't touch cache keying. Batching could — larger batches mean fewer distinct prefixes get observed early.
maria: Also note: Dedicated uses local SSD-backed memstore, Private customers often mount an NFS/remote store for KV persistence. If batch size delays first write to local cache and persistence latency is high, subsequent requests miss.
carlos: Confirmed on infra side: one Private customer showed NFS write latency spikes ~60-120ms in the same window. Hosted has a short-lived local LRU cache warm path we added last year; Dedicated was configured to rely on local memstore + background flush, Private relies on network fs sync by default. Config drift.
anya: Attached profiler snippet (simplified):
```
# prefix-pop profiler (canary):
metric: prefix_writes/s = Hosted: 112, Dedicated: 46, Private: 39
metric: prefix_reads/s  = Hosted: 268, Dedicated: 98, Private: 84
warmup_hit_rate@60s   Hosted: 0.72, Dedicated: 0.34, Private: 0.28
```
ben: Ouch. So the bigger batching reduces number of unique prefix writes early -> combined with network write latency = lower hit-rate. Kernel selection increases per-token CPU, maybe increasing per-request processing time which also stretches batch windows. Multiplicative effect.
maria: Potential short-term mitigations: 1) reduce initial batch window (back to 20) for Dedicated/Private via config override, 2) aggressive local prewarm on model start that scans recent traces to populate top-k prefixes, 3) switch Private default to async write (ack before NFS flush).
carlos: For Private, changing NFS mount options may help (noatime, async) but that needs customer coordination. We can provide a recommended fstab snippet.
ben: Can we do a quick canary rollback of the batching heuristic while we iterate? Or ship a config flag that sets `initial_batch_window_ms` per deployment class?
anya: I prefer config flag per deployment class so we don't lose token-cost benefits globally. Immediate plan:
- anya: open perf regression ticket and link profiling graphs (ETA 30m)
- ben: add `initial_batch_window_ms` override + canary to Dedicated (ETA 2h)
- carlos: draft Private/Customer NFS mount recommendations + check if we can enable async writes by default for new Private installs (ETA EOD)
- maria: prototype prewarm small top-k scan at model start (spawns background prefetch) (ETA tomorrow)
ben: Also adding a short-term smoke test: issue 1000 synthetic prefix requests with varied prefixes to measure warmup hit-rate within 60s.
deploy-bot: Deploy triggered by ben for config-flag canary -> cluster:dedicated-canary (job: runtime-config-rollout/1775551234) :rocket:
anya: Thanks — will monitor. If we see Dedicated hit-rate recover to >60% within the canary window, we keep the heuristic change but keep per-deployment initial_window tunable. Otherwise rollback.
carlos: FYI I'll also add an infra alert if NFS write p95 > 80ms for >5m for any Private customer so we catch this earlier.
maria: If anyone needs the perf traces I uploaded to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/prefix-warmup/1775551234/*.json
anya: Ping me in thread if you want direct links.
ben: TL;DR — regression caused by interaction: larger batches + kernel-induced processing time + networked backing store => slow prefix population on Dedicated/Private. Short-term: config override and infra recommendations. Long-term: smarter warmup + prioritized key prefetch. :thumbsup:
